A long queue can still leave your vacancy open. This clip, shared as a Wipro walk-in interview, shows a long line of people waiting outside an office. Picture a factory in Ludhiana hiring a shift supervisor. A candidate takes half a day off, travels to your plant and waits for a turn. Only in the interview do they learn that the job includes rotating night shifts. Where did the hiring process break? In the job ad, where the shift details belonged. The candidate loses half a day. Your production manager is still looking for someone to run the shift. Before your next walk-in, put three things in the job ad: The pay range and shift pattern. One actual job task you’ll assess. The date candidates will hear back. For a shift supervisor, try this: ask how they’d hand over a batch that’s on quality hold when the next shift takes over. I share practical ways factory owners can improve hiring and run better shifts. What’s one thing candidates for your toughest vacancy usually find out too late?
